rows.verified: Electrical hazards include shock, burns, arcing, fire, explosion and ignition of flammable vapours or dusts.
Electrical equipment and installations must be maintained to prevent danger so far as reasonably practicable.
Users should check portable equipment before use and immediately remove damaged, overheated or exposed-wiring equipment from service.
The type and frequency of electrical checks, inspections and tests should reflect the equipment, environment and previous results.

rows.source: HSE work using electrically powered equipment
rows.verified: A risk assessment should confirm that equipment is suitable for the work, environment and electrical supply and remains in good condition.

rows.source: HSE work using electrically powered equipment
rows.verified: A suitable residual current device can reduce injury risk, but a trip indicates a fault that must be investigated before reuse.
Work preparation should isolate all relevant energy sources and secure isolation against inadvertent re-energisation.
Electrical work competence should be supported by appropriate training, relevant experience and regular reassessment.
Required controls depend on voltage, energy, equipment, environment, task complexity, isolation options and worker competence.
Electrical-safety guidance is installation-, equipment- and task-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
The asbestos dutyholder must protect workers and other building users from exposure risks.
The duty to manage covers non-domestic premises and common parts of multi-occupancy domestic premises.
Dutyholders must assess whether asbestos-containing materials are present, including their amount, location and condition.
Materials should be presumed to contain asbestos unless there is strong evidence that they do not.
An up-to-date register should record the location and condition of confirmed or presumed asbestos-containing materials.
Dutyholders must assess the risk of airborne-fibre exposure from confirmed or presumed asbestos-containing materials.
The management plan should assign responsibilities, control disturbance, monitor material condition and include emergency procedures.
Information on asbestos location and condition must be available to employees, contractors, maintenance workers and others who may disturb it.
The required survey and management response depends on building responsibility, materials, accessibility, condition and planned work.
Asbestos evidence is building-, material- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure probability.
